## What this dashboard shows

- This dashboard presents the consolidated general ledger for Wipro Enterprises across multiple business units (Consumer Care & Lighting, Infrastructure Engineering, Joint Ventures) and seven source systems (including Real SAP BDC, Simulated SAP, SAP S/4HANA systems A & B, Oracle EBS, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and Tally Prime).
- Total posting volume is ₹12,364.40B in debits and ₹12,364.33B in credits across 288 GL accounts.
- The period result (P&L) shows ₹569.50B profit, with assets increasing by ₹1,122.75B, offset by liabilities up ₹283.26B and equity up ₹277.61B.

## What to report

- Journal activity is balanced with a net variance of only ₹64.4M between total debits (₹12,364.40B) and total credits (₹12,364.33B), representing 0.0005% residual due to rounding or partial-period effects.
- Period profit reached ₹569.50B, with key balance sheet movements showing assets increased ₹1,122.75B, liabilities increased ₹283.26B, and equity increased ₹277.61B.
- Major asset movements include Bank1 Main Account with a ₹403.69B positive balance, Receivables Domestic ₹146.24B, Inventory Raw Materials ₹167.72B, and Inventory Finished Goods ₹127.06B.
- Corporate Income Tax provision stands at ₹38.00B (accounts 0024033000 and 0075002000 combined).

## Watch out for

- The dashboard includes simulated data sources ("Simulated SAP" is explicitly listed), so figures from those systems should be treated as illustrative and verified before external reporting.
- Large negative balances appear in contra-accounts: Common Stock shows -₹59.93B, inventory initialization accounts show -₹162.81B cumulative (accounts 0039911000, 0039912000), and GR/IR shows -₹32.27B, indicating significant accruals or clearing items that may need reconciliation.
- Domestic Payables show a -₹142.19B balance (account 0021100000) against Domestic Receivables of ₹146.24B; verify these are not netting exposures that should be reported gross, and confirm GR/IR clearing is progressing on schedule.
- Production and inventory variance accounts show significant activity (e.g., Loss Production Variance ₹3.67B net, Input Price Variance ₹16.85B, Resource-Usage Variance -₹14.06B); investigate drivers of these variances and whether standard costs need updating.
